items.title: Protein Language Models Fail To Capture Contact Predictions Under Invariant Relabeling
items.why: This preprint (accepted to a NeurIPS 2026 workshop) tests whether protein language model contact maps reflect coevolutionary statistics. It relabels the amino-acid alphabet, which leaves Potts-style models unchanged. It is a concrete, evidence-based check on what protein language models learn, with the limits of an unreviewed preprint.
items.takeaway: Under arbitrary relabeling, ESM-2, MSA Transformer and AMPLIFY contact maps degrade, which the authors read as reliance on canonical residue identities.

items.title: Silscore: modelling siRNA potency with positional thermodynamics and data-selected nucleotide-identity terms
items.by: Giuseppe Sacco, Isabella Baldini, Riccardo Paone, Mattia Capulli, Guido Sanguinetti, Giovanni Bussi
items.why: A compact 26-parameter siRNA potency model that pairs positional thermodynamics with sparse nucleotide-identity terms, with parameters the authors say can be interpreted directly. Its evaluation across transfer settings and training sets of differing sequence similarity is worth checking. This is a preprint, and the results are the authors' own.
items.takeaway: The authors report the highest observed Pearson correlation in all three transfer evaluations, but the data support a clear advantage over every comparator only on Katoh-Suzuki.

items.title: Multimodal Neurons in Artificial Neural Networks
items.why: A careful interpretability study of CLIP neurons, with feature visualization, tuning curves and links to the neuroscience of concept cells.
items.takeaway: The article finds CLIP neurons that respond to concepts across modalities, and it examines typographic attacks.

items.title: Extrinsic Hallucinations in LLMs
items.why: A well-organized overview of how extrinsic hallucination is defined, what causes it, and how it is measured, including FActScore, SAFE and SelfCheckGPT. Useful for thinking rigorously about evaluation.
items.takeaway: Citing Gekhman et al. 2024, it reports that fine-tuning on new knowledge is learned more slowly and, once learned, increases the tendency to hallucinate.

items.title: Adaptive Parallel Reasoning: The Next Paradigm in Efficient Inference Scaling
items.why: A survey of parallel reasoning that explains how adaptive methods let the model choose when to fork threads, and how fork-join inference is implemented. The authors disclose that one of them co-led a method discussed. It is a perspective piece, so read it as a framing rather than a neutral benchmark.
items.takeaway: The post contrasts engine-modifying KV-cache stitching (Multiverse) with client-side orchestration (ThreadWeaver).

items.title: Let's build the GPT Tokenizer
items.why: A hands-on video on building a GPT tokenizer, which is how text becomes the discrete representation language models consume. It gives a build-it-yourself view of a component often treated as a black box. The page excerpt contains only the title, so the content is judged from the title and creator.

earlier.title: Probing Transformer Representations Layer by Layer, Module by Module
earlier.why: Asks which layer and which module of a transformer to probe, a concrete representation-learning question that goes beyond probing only the final layer. It is a preprint, so the results are unreviewed.
earlier.takeaway: The abstract reports that choosing the layer and module jointly beats fixing the residual stream, based on more than 144,000 linear-probing evaluations.

earlier.title: Cis -regulation and natural selection in the evolution of human DNA methylation
earlier.why: A fresh eLife paper on how cis-regulation and natural selection shape human DNA methylation, which fits the genetics and evolution interest and is outside the AI-centred items. The supplied page excerpt did not load, so only the title is known and the methods and evidence are unchecked.
